summary:
Returns a non-zero value if `arg` is a function pointer, or 0 otherwise. A function pointer is a variable of type function, for example:
   function f = (: this_player(), "query" :);
   function f = (: write, "Hello, world!\n" :);

The return value identifies the function-pointer type defined in the driver header "include/function.h".

   function pointer type        value
   ---------------------        -----
   call_other                   FP_CALL_OTHER
   lfun                         FP_LOCAL
   efun                         FP_EFUN
   simul_efun                   FP_SIMUL
   functional                   FP_FUNCTIONAL

Additional flags may be present:
   (has arguments)                 FP_HAS_ARGUMENTS
   (creating object destructed)    FP_OWNER_DESTED
   (cannot be bound)               FP_NOT_BINDABLE

These additional values are bit flags and can be tested with bitwise operations. FP_MASK masks out flags to obtain the basic pointer type.

To test whether a function pointer is an efun pointer:

   if ((functionp(f) & FP_MASK) == FP_EFUN) ...

To test whether it has arguments:

   if (functionp(f) & FP_HAS_ARGUMENTS) ...

Contents of the <function.h> header:

/* codes returned by the functionp() efun */

#define FP_LOCAL 2
#define FP_EFUN 3
#define FP_SIMUL 4
#define FP_FUNCTIONAL 5

/* internal use */
#define FP_G_VAR 6
#define FP_L_VAR 7
#define FP_ANONYMOUS 8

/* additional flags */
#define FP_MASK 0x0f
#define FP_HAS_ARGUMENTS 0x10
#define FP_OWNER_DESTED 0x20
#define FP_NOT_BINDABLE 0x40
